fusus1.definition: fūsus, a, um, Part. and P. a., from fundo. → fūsus, i, m., — I. a spindle. — I. Lit., Plin. 8, 48, 74, § 194; 11, 23, 27, § 78; 28, 2, 5, § 28; Verg. G. 4, 348; Tib. 2, 1, 64; Ov. M. 4, 221; 229; 6, 22; Prud. stef. 10, 239; Vulg. Prov. 31, 19.—An attribute of the Fates, Verg. E. 4, 46; Ov. H. 12, 4.— — II. Transf., in mechanics, a cross-bar, rundle connecting two wheels near the circumference, Vitr. 10, 6 fin.

fusus2.definition: fūsus ī, m a spindle, V., Ct., Tb., O., Iu.— Of the Fates, V., O.
